edition_subtitle: Energy, security and humanitarian pressures shape the start of the week.

summary.spotlight: Ukraine's mass drone attack on Russian oil sites coincides with a sharp dispute over U.S. sanctions. In the Middle East, shipping risks and fighting in Yemen are drawing in regional allies, while Ebola spreads in central Africa.
summary.reader_note: Reporting is current to Monday morning in Romania. Reddit discussions reflect participating users, not representative public opinion.

featured_story.label: Top Story
featured_story.headline: Ukraine hits Russian oil sites in mass drone attack
featured_story.summary: Ukrainian strikes set an oil export terminal and depot ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday during an attack involving more than 1,000 drones, AP reports. The assault came as Washington criticized Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure and delayed new sanctions on Moscow.
featured_story.why_it_matters: The attack exposes Russian energy infrastructure to further disruption while Kyiv and Washington disagree over how to pressure Moscow.

sections.title: Ukraine War
sections.description: A widening dispute over sanctions and the risks of cross-border drone operations.

stories.label: U.S. policy
stories.headline: Trump defends delaying new Russia sanctions
stories.summary: President Donald Trump defended his waiver delaying sweeping new U.S. sanctions on Russia, saying he did not want to drive Moscow away from negotiations. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has urged supporters to press for the restrictions.
stories.why_it_matters: The waiver changes the immediate pressure on Russia and underscores a divide over the path to ending the war.

stories.label: Early warning
stories.headline: Kyiv says U.S. intelligence sharing has resumed
stories.summary: Zelenskyy said U.S. intelligence sharing resumed after a pause, while restrictions affecting Ukrainian use of satellite communications remained. He attributed the restrictions to a message from the U.S. government; that account is his assertion.
stories.why_it_matters: Early warning and reliable communications are important to Ukraine's defense against Russian attacks.

stories.label: Lithuania
stories.headline: Ukraine apologizes after drone enters Lithuania
stories.summary: Lithuania told residents in parts of the country to shelter and briefly closed Kaunas airport after an object entered its airspace Sunday. Ukraine later apologized and said Russian electronic warfare may have diverted a drone; Lithuanian authorities reported no injuries.
stories.why_it_matters: The incident shows how long-range drone operations can spill into NATO airspace, even when their intended target lies elsewhere.

sections.title: Middle East
sections.description: Shipping threats, regional military support and humanitarian needs remain intertwined.

stories.label: Hormuz
stories.headline: Iran reports tanker fires after mine strikes
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state media. Reuters reported the Iranian account; the circumstances require independent confirmation.
stories.why_it_matters: The threat to tankers adds uncertainty to a critical route for global oil supplies.

stories.label: Yemen
stories.headline: Airstrike kills at least nine in rebel-held Yemen
stories.summary: An airstrike in Houthi-held Yemen killed at least nine people, AP reported Sunday, as fighting between the rebels and Saudi-backed forces intensified. The Houthis have also attacked Saudi Arabia with missiles and drones.
stories.why_it_matters: The renewed fighting threatens civilians in Yemen and risks widening the regional conflict.

stories.label: Regional alliances
stories.headline: Egypt pledges support for Saudi defense
stories.summary: Egypt's National Defense Council agreed to provide support to Saudi Arabia amid escalating Houthi attacks, without detailing the measures. President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi has requested parliamentary authorization to deploy troops and equipment abroad.
stories.why_it_matters: The pledge could deepen regional involvement, although it does not itself establish that Egyptian forces have deployed.

stories.label: Gaza
stories.headline: WFP cuts Gaza assistance as funding falls short
stories.summary: The World Food Programme says funding problems have forced it to reduce the number of people receiving aid in Gaza from 1.6 million to 1.1 million. Its acting chief warned of severe hardship as winter approaches.
stories.why_it_matters: Aid reductions affect a population that remains heavily dependent on humanitarian assistance.

stories.label: Lebanon
stories.headline: Lebanon seeks halt to Israeli attacks at U.S. talks
stories.summary: Lebanon said its military delegation would press for a halt to Israeli attacks during U.S.-brokered talks. A previous agreement links Beirut's commitment to disarm Hezbollah with a gradual Israeli withdrawal.
stories.why_it_matters: Implementation and security guarantees are central to whether the border arrangement can reduce violence.

sections.title: Health & Hunger
sections.description: Disease and food insecurity strain already vulnerable communities.

stories.label: Ebola
stories.headline: Congo outbreak reaches an eighth province
stories.summary: Congo's health ministry reported two Ebola cases, including one death, in Nord-Ubangi, the eighth province affected. Authorities have recorded at least 9,400 cases and more than 4,500 deaths in the outbreak declared in May, AP reports.
stories.why_it_matters: The geographic spread complicates contact tracing and treatment in remote border areas.

stories.label: Kenya
stories.headline: Kenya reports eighth Ebola case
stories.summary: Kenya's health authorities said a patient attendant who cared for the first patient tested positive, bringing the country's total to eight. Officials said there was no community transmission identified so far.
stories.why_it_matters: Monitoring exposed contacts and protecting health workers are critical to containing further spread.

stories.label: Sudan
stories.headline: War and drought deepen Sudan's famine risk
stories.summary: A global food-crisis monitor warned last week that conflict, drought and funding shortages are worsening food insecurity in parts of Darfur and Kordofan. Sudan's war has displaced millions and already pushed parts of the country into famine.
stories.why_it_matters: Restricted humanitarian access and crop losses threaten to intensify a prolonged crisis.

sections.title: Markets & Trade
sections.description: Oil prices, technology shares and a new trade pact shape the economic outlook.

stories.label: Markets
stories.headline: Asian markets mixed as oil retreats
stories.summary: Asian shares were mixed Monday as technology stocks remained volatile and oil fell following Washington's Russia sanctions waiver. Investors are also weighing the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence investment boom ahead of corporate earnings.
stories.why_it_matters: Energy uncertainty and expectations for AI spending remain important drivers of markets.

stories.label: Trade
stories.headline: Vietnam signs free-trade pact with EFTA
stories.summary: Vietnam and the European Free Trade Association's four members—Norway, Switzerland, Iceland and Liechtenstein—signed a free-trade agreement Sunday. The pact provides for reductions or elimination of duties on a range of goods.
stories.why_it_matters: The deal expands trade links between Southeast Asia and European economies outside the EU.

sections.title: Romania
sections.description: The Black Sea war continues to affect Romania's air and maritime security.

stories.label: Black Sea
stories.headline: Romanian F-16s shoot down two drones
stories.summary: Romanian fighter jets shot down two drones over the country's territorial waters on Saturday, the defense ministry said. Defense Minister Radu Miruță said Sunday they were likely Russian-made Geran-4 drones; the identification was an assessment.
stories.why_it_matters: The interceptions followed attacks on commercial vessels near Romania and highlight risks on NATO's eastern flank.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.description: A crowd disaster and a military training fire leave families and communities grieving.

stories.label: India
stories.headline: At least 19 die in Kolkata festival crowd crush
stories.summary: At least 19 people were killed in a crowd crush during Durga Puja celebrations in Kolkata, officials said Sunday. AP reported that people near a pavilion rushed for cover when rain began.
stories.why_it_matters: The tragedy raises urgent questions about crowd management at large public gatherings.

stories.label: Canada
stories.headline: Four soldiers die in Alberta training-base fire
stories.summary: A fast-moving grass fire overtook troops conducting live-fire training at a military base in Alberta, killing four service members and injuring 39 people, officials said Sunday. Nineteen of the injured were reported in critical condition.
stories.why_it_matters: The disaster has prompted scrutiny of the conditions and response during training.

sections.title: Trending on Reddit
sections.description: Selected discussions illustrate questions and reactions rather than representative public opinion.

stories.label: r/oil
stories.headline: Oil community discusses strikes on Russian terminals
stories.summary: A post sharing AP's reporting on the St. Petersburg strikes drew discussion of oil infrastructure and the wider energy war. The linked reporting, rather than commenters' predictions, is the basis for the reported attack.
stories.why_it_matters: The discussion shows how market-focused readers are following physical disruptions to energy supply.

stories.label: r/worldnews
stories.headline: Users discuss Ukraine's civilian casualties
stories.summary: A widely shared thread on Ukrainian civilian casualties drew discussion of the war and the U.S. sanctions decision. Comments are opinions and do not independently establish the casualty claims in the post.
stories.why_it_matters: The thread reflects attention to the human cost alongside debate over foreign policy.
